metadata.title: Flow Straight and Fast: Learning to Generate and Transfer Data with Rectified Flow (Liu, Gong, Liu, 2022)
metadata.framework: learning straight ODE transport maps via rectified flow (linear interpolation regression)
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on well-known content of arXiv:2209.03003.

nodes.name: Transport map via ODE
nodes.statement: Given source distribution $\pi_0$ (e.g., $\mathcal{N}(0,I)$) and target distribution $\pi_1$ (data), learn a velocity field $\mathbf{v}: [0,1] \times \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^d$ such that the ODE $d\mathbf{Z}_t / dt = \mathbf{v}(\mathbf{Z}_t, t)$ transports $\pi_0$ to $\pi_1$: $\mathbf{Z}_0 \sim \pi_0 \implies \mathbf{Z}_1 \sim \pi_1$.

nodes.name: Linear interpolation and rectified flow objective
nodes.statement: Given a coupling $(\mathbf{X}_0, \mathbf{X}_1)$ with $\mathbf{X}_0 \sim \pi_0$, $\mathbf{X}_1 \sim \pi_1$, define the linear interpolation $\mathbf{X}_t = (1-t)\mathbf{X}_0 + t\mathbf{X}_1$. The rectified flow objective trains $\mathbf{v}_\theta$ to match the direction of this interpolation: $\min_\theta \int_0^1 \mathbb{E} \| \mathbf{v}_\theta(\mathbf{X}_t, t) - (\mathbf{X}_1 - \mathbf{X}_0) \|^2 \, dt$. The velocity $(\mathbf{X}_1 - \mathbf{X}_0)$ is the constant velocity along the straight line from $\mathbf{X}_0$ to $\mathbf{X}_1$.

nodes.name: Rectification (reflow) procedure
nodes.statement: Rectification iteratively straightens flows. Given a learned flow $\mathbf{v}_\theta^{(k)}$, generate a new coupling $(\mathbf{X}_0^{(k+1)}, \mathbf{X}_1^{(k+1)})$ by solving the ODE from $\mathbf{X}_0 \sim \pi_0$ to get $\mathbf{X}_1 = \phi_1(\mathbf{X}_0)$. Use this new coupling to train $\mathbf{v}_\theta^{(k+1)}$. Each round of rectification reduces the transport cost and straightens the trajectories, enabling fewer discretization steps.

nodes.name: Distillation for one-step generation
nodes.statement: After rectification produces nearly straight flows, distill the multi-step ODE into a one-step map: train a network $\hat{\mathbf{v}}$ to match $\hat{\mathbf{v}}(\mathbf{X}_0) \approx \mathbf{X}_1$ (or equivalently $\hat{\mathbf{v}}(\mathbf{X}_0) \approx \mathbf{X}_1 - \mathbf{X}_0$) on the rectified coupling. This enables single-step generation.

nodes.name: Image-to-image transfer
nodes.statement: Rectified flow naturally handles distribution-to-distribution transfer (not just noise-to-data). Given paired samples $(\mathbf{X}_0, \mathbf{X}_1)$ from any two distributions, learn an ODE transport. Applications include domain transfer, style transfer, and image-to-image translation.

nodes.name: Rectification reduces transport cost
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbf{v}^{(k)}$ be the rectified flow at iteration $k$, and let $W_2^{(k)}$ be the $L^2$ Wasserstein cost of the induced coupling. Then $W_2^{(k+1)} \le W_2^{(k)}$. Rectification monotonically decreases the transport cost and increases the straightness of trajectories. In the limit, the flow converges to the optimal transport map (for the independent coupling initialization).

nodes.name: Straight flows enable few-step generation
nodes.statement: If the learned velocity field produces straight trajectories (constant velocity along each trajectory), then Euler discretization with any step size is exact. After sufficient rectification rounds, the flow is approximately straight, enabling high-quality generation with very few (1-5) Euler steps.
conclusions: Near-exact generation with few Euler steps
Orders of magnitude speedup over standard diffusion sampling

nodes.name: Image generation results
nodes.statement: Rectified Flow achieves competitive FID scores on CIFAR-10 and CelebA with significantly fewer sampling steps than diffusion models. After one round of rectification + distillation, achieves FID ~6.2 on CIFAR-10 with one-step generation.
